gaps.wanted: Whether the NCS 5002 is on sale. The one held document is silent; the intake grid marks every NCS model unknown. An end-of-sale notice or the product page would settle it.

A flat front and rear elevation, or a photograph taken square on. The guide's Figures 3 and 4 are greyscale three-quarter views, so every position is estimated and no printed numeral or legend can be read.

The width of the seam between the two stacked halves and the margin above and below the cage fields. They are read off Figure 4 as 3.0 mm and 17.5 mm from a three-quarter view, and a flat elevation would settle them to the millimetre.
The legends printed beside the ports, lamps and jacks. None is resolved in the held figures, so none is drawn, and the model name is not drawn either because nothing shows it as printed.
Which half of the face is the baseboard and which the DWDM and ZR mezzanine. The guide gives the counts and the colours and no position.

The management jack's rate. Searched the guide for "10/100", "1000", "Gigabit" and "speed" beside the management interface: it names the interface and the console's RS-232 and gives no rate for the jack.

The grounding pad. The guide says to remove "the label on the right side of the front side (port side)" of the 5002 to expose it and shows it in Figure 15 in three-quarter view; its position and size cannot be read, so it is not drawn.

The rack-mount kit as a kit contract: part numbers, the dimensions of the bracket, guide and slider rail, and the rack depth range. The guide gives a parts list (Table 9; accessory kit NCS-5002-ACSR in Appendix A) whose counts disagree, and a rack requirement of 23.5 to 34.0 in between the outside faces of the front and rear rails.
The fan module's power draw, and the chassis' own draw. Appendix C gives supply ratings only.

The air filters, which the guide draws but does not size or number. Port-side intake takes a three-piece filter on the port-side faceplate (Figure 22); port-side exhaust takes clip-on filters on the supply and fan fronts (Figure 23, drawn on this chassis's two-fan rear). No part number, size or position is held for either.
A drawing of the lid, the underside and the side walls. The guide shows them in three-quarter view only, with bracket holes on a side wall.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

which optics actually run in each pluggable cage - as prose in `attrs.optics-<media>` for now, which at least reaches the group, and structurally once enough vendors are in to say what the vocabulary has to hold

an `attrs.performance` section; `cpu`, `memory` in a missing `attrs.platform` section; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 4 bays (rear 4); `physical-context` on port groups qsfp28-lower, qsfp28-upper, sfp-plus-lower, sfp-plus-upper - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

airflow.note: Chapter 2, Airflow Direction: front-to-back is "port side intake" and back-to-front is "port side exhaust", set by the type of fan modules and power supplies, and "it is not possible to mix airflow directions". The two builds are configurations. THE GUIDE GIVES NO COLOUR FOR EITHER DIRECTION in text or in its greyscale figures (it says only that a replacement has "the same coloring as the other fan and power supply modules in the same chassis"), so no handle colour is set per configuration.

arrangement.note: READ OFF FIGURE 4 AND THE RACK-MOUNTING FIGURES 9 AND 11, which show the same face: two stacked one-rack-unit halves with a seam between them, each with two rows of cages split into two groups of equal length, a block of larger cages at the right end, and at the left a plate (upper half) and a cluster of lamps, jacks and a USB port (lower half). Twenty cages a row is the guide's 80 over four rows; ten a group is the cage count in each group of Figure 4; the 2.5 mm gutter is a guess. Two QSFP28 a half is the guide's four over two halves, drawn as one column of two. The row pitch is the registry's 15.0 mm stack figure. THE SEAM BETWEEN THE TWO PAIRS IS 3.0 MM: on Figure 4 (printed page 4) the gap between the upper half's lower row and the lower half's upper row measures about 10 px against the 310 px height of the face's near end (88.9 mm, about 3.5 px per mm), and the two pairs with that seam are centred on the face, 17.5 mm clear above and below. An earlier draft centred each pair in its half and left a 19 mm band. The measure is on a three-quarter view, so it is an estimate to a millimetre or two. The console, management jack, USB port and lamp keep their offsets from the lower pair.

colour.note: The face is a light grey with dark printing in the guide's greyscale figures; #c9cccf is chosen by eye, not sampled.

configuration-names.note: THE GUIDE GIVES NO CHASSIS PART NUMBER AND NO CODE FOR ANY BUILD. Its only orderable codes for this router are the supplies and fan modules (Tables 4 and 5) and the accessory kit NCS-5002-ACSR, and it says "power supply options need to be configured with the base chassis". The four configurations are therefore one `kind: base` build (AC, port-side intake) and three `kind: example` builds, with no `part-numbers`: each says which supplies and fan modules it seats, and none is an orderable SKU.

console-and-management.note: Two RJ-45 jacks stacked at the left of the lower half, the console over the management jack, and a USB-A port beside them, as the library draws them on other Cisco boxes. Figure 4 shows a lamp cluster, a small upright port and two stacked jacks there; the guide's text names a console, a management and a USB interface and gives no more.

dimensions.note: Appendix C, Table 12, p.41: "3.5 x 17.42 x 19.28 in. (8.9 cm x 44.3 cm x 48.97 cm)". The inch figures are carried, converted to 88.9 x 442.5 x 489.7 mm; the centimetre figures round to 44.3 and 48.97 and agree within 0.6 mm. Chapter 1 calls it "2RU form factor". Whether the width includes the rack-mount brackets is not stated; the brackets are a separate kit (Table 9) and are not drawn.

ears-and-kits.note: The `flush` position is the one Figures 9 and 11 draw: the front bracket, held by two screws to two holes, stands with its flange level with the port-side face. Its two-hole bracket differs from the 5001's four-of-six, and no other position is drawn. NO KIT IS MODELLED: Table 9 lists the rack-mount kit as four brackets, sixteen M4 screws, four rack-mount guides and two slider rails, and Appendix A lists accessory kit NCS-5002-ACSR with two of each bracket and guide, so the guide disagrees with itself on the counts; no held document gives a bracket's, a guide's or a slider's dimensions or the kit's depth range. See the gaps.

gate-1.note: FAILED AND SAID SO. Figure 4 (front) and Figure 3 (rear) are not orthographic: the near end of each face is drawn larger than the far end, so no px/mm can be derived and the aspect cannot be compared with Table 12's 442.5 by 88.9 mm. Only fractions of the face width were taken along the near edge, with a repeated feature of known size as the ruler: ten SFP cages at 14.25 mm abut for 142.5 mm, and each group of ten reads about a third of the cage field in Figure 4. Every x and y on both faces is therefore estimated; the counts are the guide's.

intake-mesh.note: NOT DRAWN. Figure 4 (printed page 4) shows no black perforated strip: the lid is plain to its front edge and the front is the two cage fields, which read dark at this resolution. The 5001's perforated strip on the lid (Figure 2) has no counterpart here, so no vent is drawn on this device. The vendor logo at the upper left stays reserved as `logo-zone`.

lamps.note: Appendix E: a "Power LED" on the front of the chassis (green solid on: system on and operating normally; green off: powered off; amber on: fault condition), and on each supply an OK lamp (green) and a FAILED lamp (amber), Tables 24 and 25. No port lamp, link lamp or fan lamp is described, so none is drawn; the chassis lamp's position is a guess at the lamp cluster in Figure 4.

lifecycle.note: SALE STATUS IS UNKNOWN. The guide, in 66 pages, says nothing about end-of-sale or end-of-life, and no other document for this model is held; a revision date is not a status. No end-of-sale date is written.

port-order.note: THE GUIDE PRINTS NO PORT NUMBER IN ANY FIGURE AND NONE IS RESOLVED IN THE ARTWORK, so no numeral is drawn. The ids port-1 to port-40 (upper SFP+), port-41 to port-80 (lower SFP+), port-81 and port-82 (upper QSFP28) and port-83 and port-84 (lower QSFP28) follow the library's convention for stacked cages, down each column with the upper cage first. That order is a choice and not a reading. Interface names (the guide does not give them for the 5002) are not recorded.

ports.note: Chapter 1, Ports: "80 x One GE/10GE SFP+ ports", of which "40 x Regular 10G SFP+ Ports, on baseboard" and "40 x DWDM and ZR Capable 10G SFP+ Ports, on mezzanine (Cisco Metallic Grey in color)", and "4 x 100G QSFP28 ports (Light Green in color)". WHICH HALF OF THE FACE IS THE BASEBOARD AND WHICH THE MEZZANINE IS NOT STATED, and the groups are named for where they sit, upper and lower. Features: "A management, console, and the USB interface on the port (front) side of the router". Appendix D: the console is "an asynchronous RS-232 serial port with an RJ-45 connector". The guide describes no timing port; none is modelled.

rear-face.note: Figure 3 (back, fan side), left to right as drawn: a plate over a power supply, two fan modules each the full two units tall, a plate over a power supply. The supplies sit in the lower half and a blank plate fills the half above each. Module widths are fractions of the face width along its near edge: a supply reads about a quarter, a fan module about a quarter. Nothing is on the rear but these four modules and the plates: the console, management and USB ports are on the port side. The plates above the supplies carry a label; its text is not resolved and it is not drawn.

sources.note: One document: Hardware Installation Guide for Cisco NCS 5000 Series Routers, first published 2015-12-23, last modified 2019-01-31 (https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/iosxr/ncs5000/hardware-install/b-ncs5000-hardware-installation-guide.pdf). It is an old revision and a newer one may exist. HELD AND SEARCHED FOR THIS MODEL: the guide's text and figures, and the intake notes for the NCS line. NOT HELD: a data sheet, a NetBox device type or elevation, a photograph, a 3D model. THE GUIDE'S FACE FIGURES (3 and 4) ARE GREYSCALE THREE-QUARTER VIEWS at 1013 x 228 and 770 x 506 px; there is no flat front or rear panel figure, so every position below is read off a perspective drawing.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (the upper cage upright over the lower turned 180) in each half, by the rule and not by observation: Figure 4's resolution does not show which way the cages' lips face.

weight.note: Table 12: "Cisco NCS 5002 with two 650W power supplies, and two fan modules, 46 lb (20.9 kg)", and Chapter 2 says "46 lbs". Both are a loaded weight, so no empty-chassis weight is written.
